## Included in Platform EPCI

The agreed methodology includes central-platform transport, offshore installation, hook-up and commissioning in the combined [Platform EPCI CAPEX](../platforms/platform_material_capex.qmd) package. This page explains the cost boundary and the decision to stop calculating platform installation as a separate additive cost.

The combined commercial relationship is intended to scale with hosted equipment mass, using a consistent conversion where reference data report complete topside mass. Approximately linear scaling is a hypothesis over a comparable design range; additional commercial references will be used to test it and, if justified, fit a scaling exponent. It is not a claim that every installation activity is proportional to mass.

This decision concerns central-platform installation only. [Turbine and Foundation Installation](turbine_and_foundation_installation.qmd) and [Cable and Pipeline Installation](cable_and_pipeline_installation.qmd) retain their separate scopes.

## The Previous Parametric Approach

The original method represented piled-jacket installation, topside placement and offshore hook-up as separate campaigns. Its cost structure was

$$
C_{\mathrm{inst}}
=C_{\mathrm{mob}}
+r_{FJ}T_{FJ}+r_ST_S+r_HT_H
+C_{\mathrm{exceptional}}.
$$

$C_{\mathrm{mob}}$ was mobilisation and demobilisation cost; $r_{FJ}$, $r_S$ and $r_H$ were complete-spread rates in EUR/day for foundation/jacket, topside and hook-up work; $T_{FJ}$, $T_S$ and $T_H$ were chargeable campaign days. $C_{\mathrm{exceptional}}$ represented separately defined exceptional work. All monetary terms required a common price basis and non-overlapping inclusions.

Durations combined net site work with transport and campaign logistics. An explicit topside-module count represented multiple lifts, and crane-capacity screening rejected an unsuitable installation class. Published planning durations provided some support for this structure [@boem2021CVOWCOP], but not a complete transferable set of commercial assumptions.

## Why It Is Not Costed Separately

We lack a consistently bounded set of complete-spread rates, mobilisation costs, logistics durations and commissioning assumptions for the reference platforms. Public EPCI awards do not disclose enough of their installation component to calibrate those terms independently. Populating the decomposition would therefore add uncertain assumptions without demonstrating better accuracy.

Commercial offshore EPCI already prices fabrication, integration and installation together [@petrofac2023Framework]. Under the adopted mass-driver hypothesis, the total package is the useful modelling boundary. Adding vessel campaigns to that price would double-count installation. The difference between a structural estimate and an EPCI award must not be labelled installation cost: it also contains other delivery scope and commercial differences.

Benchmark exclusions still matter. Unusual seabed preparation, exceptional foundation work or a different installation method cannot silently be assumed covered by a generic package. Such cases require a matched reference or an explicitly documented scope adjustment.

## Feasibility Remains Separate from Pricing

One central platform does not imply one topside lift. Module arrangement, maximum lifted mass, crane configuration and radius, transport, stability and weather conditions still determine whether a proposed design can be installed. Passing a simple mass-capacity screen does not establish a feasible lift plan.

A switch between crane lifting, float-over or another installation method may introduce a cost discontinuity. It is an applicability limit for the smooth EPCI relationship, not evidence for increasing platform count or applying an arbitrary correction factor.

## Preservation and Implementation Status

The full previous methodology, calculation module and scalar inputs have been copied to a dated repository archive excluded from website rendering and publication. They are retained for later use if adequate separate cost evidence becomes available.

**The combined EPCI calculation is implemented.** The live central-platform workflow books installation within the single platform EPCI entry and no longer calls the separate platform installation cost module. Legacy functions remain available for comparison only. No lift plan is inferred or certified by the EPCI calculation. Platform decommissioning has a separate unresolved input; it is not estimated as a fraction of the whole EPCI package.
